Maintenance record — 30 October 2026

Source: MAINTENANCE.md

Purpose and acceptance criteria

Native R chess play, analysis and study, with an optional external UCI engine.

The current milestone requires correct supported rules, bounded/validated inputs, meaningful failure-path regressions, an installable source package, and a working local app. Original checkouts and unrelated work are preserved in isolated review branches. No release, push or deployment is implied by this local record.

Evidence-led findings and repairs

  • High: R/play.R included an en-passant target in repetition identity even when no legal capture existed. Normalize that field against legal moves, including pinned pawns; regression positions distinguish both cases (FIDE 9.2.3).
  • Medium: R/search.R silently ignored depth on the UCI path. Forward the depth and retain a bounded one-second request; a fake engine records and checks the actual protocol.
  • Medium: non-finite/fractional counts caused coercion failures or unbounded work. Validate before conversion and avoid integer overflow in the ply limit.
  • Medium: seeded puzzles changed the caller’s RNG when optional withr was absent. Preserve and restore the base RNG explicitly.
  • Documentation: replace unsupported competitor comparisons and exhaustive-correctness language with the actual reference-position coverage.

Rule source checked: https://handbook.fide.com/chapter/E012023

Roadmap and completion

  1. Essential repairs: correct the confirmed rule/process defects above and protect them with independent boundary cases. Implemented and locally validated.
  2. Everyday use: preserve user state, validate invalid inputs, install the package, exercise play/analysis and the app. Completed for the paths below.
  3. Release preparation: synchronize documentation and package checks. Local candidate prepared; platform CI and maintainer publication review remain.
  4. Deferred enhancements: retain the focused supported model; do not add engines, rule variants or infrastructure without an explicit use case and validation.

Actual verification

R 4.6.1 on ARM64 macOS, 30 October 2026:

  • Final source-package build/check, including vignettes: Status OK, 897 assertions, 19 conditional skips; no test failures or warnings. Full source testing additionally exercised non-CRAN paths.
  • Fresh installed-package journey: fool’s mate, FEN/PGN round trips, Sicilian identification, deterministic puzzles with RNG restoration, and legal search output passed.
  • Installed Shiny app in Chromium: human move and engine reply, transfer to study, openings, puzzle hint and new-game reset passed with no page errors.

Exact command results and logs are retained locally in /Users/rh/Documents/GitHub/.repository-audit/2026-10-30-rheller-refinement/gambitR/. Failures preceding fixes remain there alongside the final evidence.

First use from this checkout

Install R (tested with 4.6.1). For compiled dependencies use Xcode command-line tools on macOS, Rtools on Windows, or the matching Linux C/C++ toolchain. From this repository, install dependencies and the local candidate:

Rscript --vanilla -e 'install.packages("remotes", repos="https://cloud.r-project.org"); remotes::install_local(".", dependencies=TRUE, upgrade="never", build_vignettes=FALSE)'
Rscript --vanilla -e 'gambitR::gm_run_app()'

Open the local URL printed by Shiny. The README gives the scriptable workflow. To repeat source tests, run Rscript --vanilla -e 'pkgload::load_all(); testthat::test_local(stop_on_failure=TRUE)' after installing the development dependencies.

Limits and next release action

A real Stockfish binary was unavailable: the client protocol was tested with a controlled external-process fixture, not a real engine. Deep perft is finite reference coverage, not a formal correctness proof. Windows/Linux and hosted CI were not rerun.

Review the local diff and run required platform CI on the chosen release commit; then decide whether to publish. No hosted result or external acceptance is claimed.
